metadata.title: PGSD Eccentricity Demonstration Reproducibility Package v1.1
metadata.description:
Version 1.1 - corrected reference-sphere geometry

This repository provides the data, analysis code, numerical outputs, and documentation required to reproduce the center-eccentricity demonstration presented in the manuscript:

“Physics-Guided Scientific Discovery (PGSD): A Reference Architecture for Explainable Knowledge Generation in Mechanical Engineering.”

Version 1.1 supersedes version 1.0. It corrects the reference-sphere diameter from 24.9984 mm to 24.98484 mm and consequently updates the effective probe-center contact radius to:

R_e = 15.49242 mm.

The original CNC measurement files are preserved unchanged. The correction affects the contact-geometry constants, the constant-radius interpretation, and the calculated higher-order contact scale. It does not change the first-order LFH differential coefficient pair because those coefficients are estimated from the measured-coordinate columns and angular directions.

The demonstration uses two CNC touch-probing acquisitions of the reference sphere, denoted X0Y0 and LT_X0Y0, each containing 32 equatorial measurement points. A nominal relative offset of (-0.300, -0.300) mm was introduced through the CNC/G54 command between the two acquisitions.

The package includes:

  • the original CNC measurement files in CMM format;
  • normalized coordinate datasets;
  • Python scripts for Local Fourier Harmonic analysis and circle fitting;
  • numerical results corresponding to the manuscript;
  • files used to reproduce Figure 4;
  • documentation of the coordinate convention, units, sampling sequence, contact-geometry constants, and execution procedure;
  • a version history and correction note;
  • a package manifest and SHA-256 checksums.

The package reproduces the first-order LFH differential coefficient pair:

  • Delta a1 = -0.299865 mm
  • Delta b1 = -0.300743 mm

and the corresponding provisional inferred magnitude of 0.424695 mm. Using the corrected effective contact radius, the characteristic second-order contact scale is 2.90465 micrometres.

The nominal CNC/G54-commanded offset was not independently measured using an external calibrated displacement reference. Therefore, the numerical differences between the LFH estimate and the nominal command must not be interpreted as independently verified displacement errors. Only one acquisition was available for each state, and no complete uncertainty budget, within-state repeatability study, or multi-state validation was performed. The reported coefficient pair is consequently classified as a physically and operationally corroborated Candidate Signature, not as a validated or canonical Signature.

Changes from version 1.0

  • corrected the reference-sphere diameter to 24.98484 mm;
  • updated the effective contact radius to 15.49242 mm;
  • updated the higher-order contact-scale calculation to 2.90465 micrometres;
  • updated the analysis documentation, numerical metadata, and checksums;
  • preserved the original CMM measurement files;
  • confirmed that the first-order LFH differential coefficients and provisional inverse estimate remain unchanged.

This package supports Section 6 of the PGSD Foundation Preprint v1.2.

metadata.title: AnytimeMonitor: an adaptive controller for TTS-MOS listening tests
metadata.description: AnytimeMonitor is an adaptive controller for Mean Opinion Score (MOS) listening tests in text-to-speech evaluation. It watches a test while it runs and reports, for every pair of systems, whether the accumulated data already supports a verdict — separated, equivalent, or continue — and, when more data is needed, which lever (more items or more listeners) closes the pair fastest. The statistical core is an anytime-valid confidence sequence (Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe & Sekhon, 2021) on per-item paired score differences, so the analyst may inspect verdicts as often as they like and stop at any data-dependent time while keeping valid coverage. Ships with a Streamlit demo UI (preloaded examples + CSV upload). Research prototype (v0.9) accompanying the paper Doing MOS—and its alternatives—well (Chevelu & Barbot; Computer Speech & Language, Special Issue on the evaluation of speech and speech synthesis).

metadata.title: The Relationship of Emotional Intelligence and Self-Efficacy on Stress Management of Gen Z Students
metadata.description:
Abstract. Generation Z students face increasing academic and emotional demands in today’s digital learning environment, making it essential to examine psychological factors that support effective stress management. Emotional intelligence (EI) and self‑efficacy are identified as key constructs influencing students’ ability to cope with academic challenges, yet their combined impact remains underexplored in Philippine higher education contexts. This study employed a quantitative descriptive‑correlational design to investigate the relationships among EI, self‑efficacy, and stress management among 100 first‑year engineering students from private universities in Cavite. Standardized instruments—including the Brief Emotional Intelligence Scale, General Self‑Efficacy Scale, and Brief‑COPE—were utilized. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression. Findings revealed high levels of emotional intelligence and very high self‑efficacy, while stress management was at a moderate level. Emotional intelligence demonstrated a significant positive relationship with stress management and emerged as a significant predictor. In contrast, self‑efficacy showed no significant relationship with stress management and did not significantly predict it when combined with EI. Additionally, EI and self‑efficacy were not significantly correlated. The results highlight EI as a crucial determinant of effective stress management, emphasizing the importance of emotional regulation and coping flexibility among Gen Z students. Although students possess strong confidence, self‑efficacy alone does not ensure effective stress management without emotional competence. The study concludes that enhancing emotional skills may better support students’ well‑being and academic success. Recommendations include integrating socio‑emotional learning interventions and stress management programs in educational settings.

Keywords: Emotional Intelligence; Generation Z; Self-Efficacy; Stress’ Stress Management

metadata.title: The Association between Teacher Engagement and Work–Life Balance among College English Teachers in Jilin Province, China
metadata.description: This study examined the association between teacher engagement and work–life balance (WLB) among college English teachers in Jilin Province, China, with particular attention to whether engagement accounts for additional variance in WLB beyond demographic characteristics. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from college English teachers working in public and private higher-education institutions in Jilin Province, and 240 valid questionnaires were retained after data-quality screening. Teacher engagement was measured using the nine-item Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9), while WLB was assessed using the four-item Work–Life Balance scale developed by Brough et al. Data were analysed in SPSS through descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, and hierarchical multiple regression, with gender, teaching experience, academic title, weekly teaching hours, and institution type entered as control variables. The results showed that teacher engagement was positively and significantly associated with WLB. Hierarchical regression further indicated that engagement explained additional variance in WLB after demographic factors were controlled, suggesting that more engaged teachers tended to report more favourable perceptions of work–life balance. Although the cross-sectional design does not permit causal inference, the findings highlight teacher engagement as an important psychological resource related to teachers’ work–life experiences. By focusing on a regional higher-education EFL teaching context and modelling engagement as an explanatory resource beyond demographic characteristics, this study extends evidence on the engagement–WLB relationship among Chinese college English teachers and provides implications for engagement-supportive institutional practices.
keywords: teacher engagement; work–life balance; college English teachers; Chinese higher education

metadata.title: Personal Factors as Predictors of Enhancing Drug-Use Intention among Athletes in Private Universities, Osun State
metadata.description: Using illegal drugs and techniques to artificially boost performance is therefore immoral and goes against the idea of fair play, damages sports ideals and puts the athletes’ health at risk. Despite this, previous studies focused mainly on enhancing drug-use, with little concentration on enhancing drug-use intention and related factors, specifically among student athletes of private universities. This study, therefore, examined personal factors as predictors of enhancing drug-use intention among athletes in private universities, Osun State. One hundred and sixty-five (165) student athletes from four (4) private universities were sampled in Osun State. Descriptive research desigh was adopted. A self-developed and validated questionnaire was used as an instrument for data collection. Pearson product-moment correlation and multiple regression analysis were used to analyse the hypotheses at the 0.05 level of significance. Results showed that experience (r=0.750) and athletes’ attitude (r=0.863) had a significant positive relationship with enhancing drug-use intentions among universities’ athletes in Osun State. There was a significant joint prediction of personal factors (experience and athletes’ attitude) on enhancing drug-use intention (F(2,162)=250.323, p<0.05). There were significant relative predictions of experience (ß=0.177, t=2.775, p<0.05) and athletes' attitude (ß=0.772, t=11.330, p<0.05) on enhancing drug-use intention among the private universities’ athletes. It was concluded in this study that experience and athletes’ attitude had a positive relationship with enhancing drug-use intentions.It was recommended among others that the authorities of private universities in Osun State should organize periodic sensitization programmes on the adverse effects of drug-use on the body system, specifically for student athletes.

metadata.title: Economic Factors as Predictors of Health Risk Behaviours among In-school Adolescents in Ibadan South East Local Government Area, Oyo State
metadata.description: Health risk behaviour (HRBs) contribute to the leading causes of mortality and morbidity among adults and youths worldwide. There is dearth of studies on HRBs related factors, specifically among in-school adolescents. Therefore, the study investigated the economic factors as predictors of health risk behaviours among in-school adolescents in Ibadan South East Local Government Area, Oyo State. Genetically Potential / Deprivation Theory and Theory of Reasoned Action were used as theories in this study. This study adopted a descriptive survey design. 257 in-school adolescent were sampled using multistage sample procedure. A self-developed and validated questionnaire was used as instrument for data collection and the reliability coefficient of the instrument yielded 0.8. Data was analysed using both descriptive and inferential statistics of multiple regression. Result revealed that economic factors of health care cost and household income were tested significant (F(4,254)=116.473, p<0.05) on health risk behaviours. Health care cost (β=-0.868, p<0.05) and household income (β=0.717, p<0.05) were independently tested significant. It was concluded that economic factors such as health care cost and household income influences health risk behaviours among in-school adolescents in Ibadan South East Local Government Area. The study recommended that periodic awareness programme should also be designed and implemented how economic factors can influence health risk behaviours among in-school adolescents in the study area.

metadata.title: An Ontology-Based Interoperability Framework for Educational Data Integration
metadata.description:
OBIF-EDI: Synthetic Dataset, Ontology and Measurement Notebook for Educational Data Interoperability Evaluation

This record provides the synthetic dataset, OWL ontology, and measurement notebook accompanying the paper "OBIF-EDI: An Ontology-Based Interoperability Framework for Educational Data Integration."

Dataset. The dataset contains 9,165 first-year student records from 13 establishments of Mohammed V University, constructed from official enrollment figures published by the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur, de la Recherche Scientifique et de l'Innovation (MESRSI) for Academic Year 2024-2025 (10% proportional sample, seed=42). It covers six CSV files — LMS learners, SIS students, courses, MOOC runs, xAPI/IMS Caliper activities (64,646 records), and IoT attendance sessions (32,139 records) — implementing six semantic alignment bridges (AR-01 to AR-06) across seven educational system types.

Ontology. The OWL 2 DL ontology (27 classes, 213 triples) formalises the educational domain and encodes six SWRL alignment rules derived from a systematic literature review of 142 empirical studies. Consistency verified with HermiT 1.4.3 under Protégé 5.5.

Notebook. A Google Colab notebook implements the full OBIF-EDI evaluation pipeline: Knowledge Graph construction, REST API measurement (100 real HTTP iterations per scenario), and automated figure and table export. Results are reported as means over 6 independent sessions: SC=94.47%, IS=0.9779, RT=14.72 ± 2.13 ms, SI=0.977 ± 0.21.

Contents. Synthetic dataset (6 CSV files), OWL 2 DL ontology, and measurement notebook.

License. CC BY 4.0.

Citation. Please cite the associated article when using this dataset, ontology, or notebook.

metadata.title: OntoAligner-Ensemble: Voting-Based Fusion across Heterogeneous Ontology Alignment Techniques
metadata.description: This repository contains the code, baseline runners, and evaluation workflows for OntoAligner-Ensemble, a modular framework for cross-paradigm ontology alignment. We present a controlled evaluation combining predictions from lexical matchers, Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) models, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines powered by open-weight and API-based LLMs (including OpenAI, Gemini, and Qwen variants). The framework features a two-stage integration process using voting-based fusion strategies (such as Weighted Voting, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, Condorcet, and Borda Count) paired with post-fusion selection policies to reconcile complementary and conflicting predictions across eight benchmarks from five OAEI tracks. The repository includes baseline and ensemble runners, configuration files, dataset handlers, and output metrics supporting reproducible cross-paradigm ontology alignment experiments.

metadata.title: From Paternity Leave to Parental Responsibility: Comments on Brazil's Law No 15,371/2026
metadata.description: This article examines the legal significance of Brazil's Law No. 15,371/2026, which introduced the most comprehensive reform of paternity leave since the adoption of the 1988 Federal Constitution. Moving beyond a descriptive analysis of the legislation, the study investigates whether the reform represents a meaningful step towards substantive gender equality and greater alignment with international labour standards. The research adopts a doctrinal legal methodology based on bibliographical and documentary analysis of Brazilian legislation, International Labour Organization (ILO) instruments, the European Union Work-Life Balance Directive (Directive (EU) 2019/1158), and relevant academic literature. The article argues that the reform transforms paternity protection by integrating labour law and social security through the creation of a contributory paternity benefit, strengthening employment protection, and extending legal safeguards to adoption and other family situations. These developments reflect the principles established by ILO Convention No. 156 concerning workers with family responsibilities and contribute to the objectives of decent work and gender equality embodied in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Nevertheless, the absence of a comprehensive shared parental leave scheme, the limited duration of leave, and the continued unequal distribution of unpaid care work demonstrate that significant legal and institutional challenges remain before substantive equality can be fully achieved.
